title: Chalazion removal
what: A chalazion is a firm lump on the eyelid from a blocked gland. Under local numbing, the doctor opens it and clears it out.
why: When the lump does not go away on its own in a few weeks, bothers you, grows, or often gets inflamed.
tell_doctor: How long you have had the lump and if it is changing
If you had a chalazion before

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Your doctor will say if anything needs to change.

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: You may have an eye patch afterward. Best not to drive.

bring: Someone to drive you, if you go by car
steps: The eyelid is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing shot is given into the eyelid
A clamp holds the eyelid still
Most often a small cut is made on the inside of the eyelid
Ointment and a pressure patch are applied
feel: The shot is unpleasant, but brief
Afterward, mild swelling and a bruise on the eyelid
after: The patch comes off after a few hours, as your doctor says
Use ointment or drops as prescribed
Swelling usually goes down in a few days
red_flags: Growing swelling, redness and pain, or a fever

faq.q: Can it go away on its own?
faq.a: Sometimes, yes. Warm compresses and eyelid massage help. Ask your doctor how to do them.
Usually the cut is on the inside of the eyelid, and no scar shows.
It can. Your doctor will explain eyelid care.

reminders.text: Chalazion removal tomorrow. Come without eye makeup.
